newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian parties fail to agree election law.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parties fail to agree election law.

text.p: Albania's political parties failed to agree a new election law on Monday, missing a planned deadline, although talks were expected to continue on Tuesday, a European security official said.

The official, from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), told Reuters that the stumbling block remained a decision on how many seats would be decided by proportional representation and how many by a simple majority vote in the planned June 29 poll.

The law is aimed at paving the way for new elections in the Balkan state, seen as vital to prevent it sliding once more into the violence that came in February and March after the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
A new election law was part of a six-point contract brokered by OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky last week and signed by the 10 main political parties.
The contract said the new law should be agreed on Monday and approved this week by parliament so that President Sali Berisha can sign an election decree by May 15.

The division of seats to be decided by a proportional or majority vote is one of the main issues that has divided Berisha's Democratic Party and the rest of the nine-party Government of National Reconciliation set up after the rioting.
